issue.title: After-commit hook failure can strand a shared repo mid-rebase with no follow-up owner
issue.description:
A failing after-commit hook can strand a shared repository mid-rebase with no follow-up owner, and the stranded state then poisons the next agent run that touches the repo.

Observed 2026-09-06 in project gh_bobs-org__bob-cli, run 20260906140830 (artifact: finalizers/commit/attempt-1.chezmoi.stderr): the chezmoi repo's after-commit hook `chezmoi update -a --force` ran `git pull --rebase` inside the canonical checkout `/home/bryan/.local/share/chezmoi`, which held an unpushed local commit (3d222f06 "chore: initialize sase memory"). The replay conflicted, the hook exited 1, and the stitch printed "Fix the after-hook failure, then run `sase stitch create --resume`" — but nothing ever acted on that instruction, so the repo sat in a paused `rebase-merge` for 30+ minutes.

The stranded state then broke an unrelated run in project gh_sase-org__sase (run 20260906142017, agent 0gr--code): its finalizer stitched the same canonical repo, dispatch failed benignly ("No staged changes to commit"), the pre-existing rebase made the workflow misclassify it as a fresh conflict, and the run failed in the resume path. (That downstream cascade has its own fix plan; this bead is about the stranding itself.)

Two distinct gaps to consider:
1. The after-hook failure path (workflow.py after-hook handling) leaves the repo in the paused VCS state and only prints an instruction; there is no repair turn, gate, or notification obligating anyone to resume, unlike the conflict-repair path for dispatch conflicts.
2. Hook design: `chezmoi update -a --force` as an after-commit hook does a pull --rebase in a repo that other projects and agents also commit to; any unpushed local commit there turns a routine hook run into a stranded rebase. The hook config may belong to another project, but the sase after-hook contract is what allows a hook to leave VCS state paused without escalation.

task_type_fields.impact: Any later agent run in any project that touches the stranded repo inherits broken VCS state; on 2026-09-06 this failed the unrelated run 20260906142017 (gh_sase-org__sase) after all its real work had landed.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/workflows/commit/workflow.py after-commit-hook failure path; chezmoi update -a --force hook
task_type_fields.repro: In a git repo with an unpushed local commit and a remote that has since advanced with conflicting changes, run a sase stitch whose after-commit hook performs 'git pull --rebase' (e.g. chezmoi update -a --force). The hook fails mid-rebase, sase prints 'Fix the after-hook failure, then run sase stitch create --resume', and the repo stays paused in rebase-merge indefinitely.
